sections.h2: What route gets a Yonkers house sold fastest?
sections.html:
Owners can hire a broker, sell privately, or deal with a cash buyer who takes the house in its present condition. One cost to plan for is a city transfer tax of 1.5 percent of the price, charged to the seller above the state's own tax.

Yonkers lies in Westchester County just north of the Bronx. Federal estimates put its population at 212,603 for July 1, 2025, the highest of any city in the county. Delays usually trace to three items: the city's property files, the tax installments, and a transfer tax return that must be stamped before the deed is recorded.

sections.h2: Who owns and who rents in Yonkers?
sections.html:
Owners are the minority here, so apartment buildings and small multifamily houses make up a large share of what trades.

Roughly nine in ten residents had not moved in the prior year. Whoever buys a house with tenants will want the leases and rent records, so assemble them before showing the property.

sections.h2: What is the layout of Yonkers, and how did it develop?
sections.html:
The city has about 18 square miles of dry land. The Hudson River forms its western edge, the Bronx River sets it apart from Mount Vernon, Tuckahoe, Bronxville and Scarsdale on the east, and the Bronx begins at its southern line. Streets climb from near sea level at the riverbank to 416 feet at Sacred Heart Church, which earned Yonkers the nickname City of Seven Hills. The Saw Mill River splits the city into four quarters and meets the Hudson at Getty Square, the downtown and civic center.

A Dutch land grant of 1645 to Adriaen van der Donck started it, and the name comes from his local title, Jonkheer. A village charter followed in 1854 and a city charter in 1872. The Otis Elevator Company opened the world's first elevator factory here after 1853, and the Alexander Smith carpet mills grew to more than 4,000 workers. Yonkers stayed out of the 1898 consolidation that created the five boroughs.

  • Northeast: Crestwood, Colonial Heights, Cedar Knolls and Lawrence Park West, close to several Metro-North stations.
  • Northwest: Nepera Park, Runyon Heights, Homefield, Glenwood and Greystone, with Victorian houses and views of the Palisades.
  • Southeast: Dunwoodie and the McLean Avenue area, where buildings recall the Bronx and Queens.
  • Southwest: Getty Square, Park Hill, Nodine Hill, Lowerre and Hudson Park, a blend of apartments, row houses and detached homes.

sections.h2: How do trains, employers and flooding history shape a Yonkers sale?
sections.html:
Rail is a big draw. Hudson Line trains stop at Ludlow, Yonkers, Glenwood and Greystone on the way to Manhattan, Amtrak's Empire Service calls at the Yonkers station, and Harlem Line stops lie along the eastern boundary. Among US cities Yonkers ranks eleventh for transit ridership, and 27 percent of households own no car. Highway links include I-87 and the Saw Mill, Bronx River, Sprain Brook and Cross County parkways.

The city's 2024 annual financial report lists these major employers: St. John's Riverside Hospital with 1,939 jobs, St. Joseph's Medical Center with 1,027, then Liberty Lines, Kawasaki Rail, Consumer Reports and Lionsgate. On September 29, 2023, flash flooding brought a local state of emergency, and crews pumped water from homes afterward. A basement that took water will draw questions from the buyer's inspector and insurer, so keep repair receipts.

sections.h2: What does the Yonkers Department of Housing and Buildings handle?
sections.html:
The department grants building permits and certificates of occupancy, inspects work and looks into complaints. Applications are filed online through City Squared.

  • A permit to renovate an existing dwelling for one to three families requires a Home Improvement Contractor's License, which the Consumer Protection Bureau issues.
  • Property files are reviewed by appointment, so have the block and lot at hand. The department is digitizing paper records and emails a link in place of an office visit.
  • The link may arrive after the appointment date, which is a reason to ask early.

Older Yonkers houses commonly have additions and finished basements, and the file is where a buyer's attorney checks for matching permits.

sections.h2: How does the Yonkers property tax bill work?
sections.html:
Homeowners receive two bills. The county bill comes in March and is paid in a single payment, due in April (April 14 in 2026). The City and School bill comes in July and is divided into three equal installments.

  • First installment, 2026/27: Friday, July 24, 2026, already past.
  • Second: Tuesday, October 6, 2026, also past.
  • Third: Wednesday, January 6, 2027.

The first date falls 30 days after the city adopts its budget. The second and third are set at October 6 and January 6, shifted off weekends. Yonkers offers no grace period. Late installments earn 15 percent annual interest, figured daily from the confirmation date, and the city says it cannot forgive that interest. The envelope postmark decides whether a mailed payment was on time.

Title and mortgage companies may research parcels free online or order a Tax Office search at $5 per property per year, with a two to three week lead time. Payments go to City Hall, Room 108, at 40 South Broadway.

sections.h2: When can you contest a Yonkers assessment?
sections.html:
The Assessment Department keeps a fixed calendar, and the filing period lasts only two weeks.

  • October 15: taxable status date, and the last day to file or renew senior, disability and veterans exemptions.
  • November 1: tentative roll published.
  • November 1 to 15: complaints go to the Board of Assessment Review.
  • December 15: cutoff for added information or a personal hearing request.
  • Last Monday in January to the third Friday in February: hearings.
  • April 10: final roll. Owners who protested can seek Small Claims Assessment Review through the county from April 10 to May 10.

The period closes on November 15 every year, and anyone who misses it waits twelve months.

sections.h2: What do Yonkers sellers pay at closing?
sections.html:
The city tax is 1.5 percent of the selling price and falls on the seller. Sales of $25,000 or less owe nothing, and co-op units are exempt. The payment is due within seven days after the deed is handed over and before it is recorded. Seller and buyer each file a return, even if no tax is owed.

The order of steps: file the return, pay, collect the stamped receipt, then bring that receipt to the Westchester County Clerk when the deed is recorded. The city says email is quickest for getting the stamp, and mailed copies go to City Hall, Room 108.

Applied to the $501,600 typical home value, the city charge works out to $7,524. The state's base tax would add $2,008 on the price rounded to $502,000. Form TP-584 goes to the county clerk within 15 days of delivery, and the buyer owes a 1 percent mansion tax once a residence reaches $1 million.

faqs.q: What does Yonkers transfer tax cost on a $500,000 house?
faqs.a: It comes to $7,500, which is 1.5 percent of the price. The seller pays the city within seven days after the deed is delivered and before it is recorded.

faqs.q: When is the next Yonkers City tax installment due?
faqs.a: Wednesday, January 6, 2027, for the third installment of the 2026/27 bill. The July 24 and October 6, 2026 dates have already passed.

faqs.q: Does Yonkers add interest if a payment is a day late?
faqs.a: Yes. With no grace period, interest of 15 percent a year accrues from the confirmation date, figured daily, and the city says it cannot be waived.

faqs.q: How do I see the building file for my Yonkers house?
faqs.a: Book an appointment with the Department of Housing and Buildings and supply the block and lot. The department then emails a link to its paper and digital records.

faqs.q: Which office records a Yonkers deed?
faqs.a: The Westchester County Clerk does. Yonkers stamps its own transfer tax receipt first, and that receipt goes to the clerk along with the deed.
